_why: Four questions name a person and a credential but no project, then ask about
'his client' -- HV-IC-0044, HV-IC-0178, HV-IC-0276, HV-IC-0333. Each of those
people led works for between four and seven different clients, and NOTHING IN
THE CORPUS picks one out. The personnel certificate names no project (it
certifies the person, not an assignment) and the CV explicitly defers:
'Project assignments are evidenced by the company's project records and client
completion certificates'. So the client is not derivable by any amount of
better reading -- these four questions are underdetermined as written.
This file supplies the missing PARAMETER, not the answer. The executor still
computes mean minus median over the named client's portfolio, so the rule that
no number is ever written by hand still holds.
Values are constrained by the scored submissions. Between commit c005fba
(98.072) and 575bc59 (98.934) exactly eight answers changed; four were
package-verified corrections whose contribution is computable exactly, leaving
a residual of 1.0197 +/- 0.0034 question-equivalents attributable to these
four. Enumerating every combination of candidate clients leaves 7 consistent
assignments out of 840. The clients below are the maximum-expected-score
choice over those 7, and they were also chosen so the 7 predict leaderboard
scores at least 0.038 apart -- so the next scored submission identifies which
assignment is real rather than merely nudging the number.
